text_fidelity_a:
Gelindo Tactical Backpack with Bladder - Insulated Military Pack with Molle System I bought this for my fiancé for Christmas, he needed a new emergency backpack. You never really know what you’re getting when you’re ordering stuff like this online...one review will say it’s garbage, the next will say it’s the best thing ever. I’m pretty good at judging which ones are accurate, and which ones are super-biased - either for or against.

This is a very good backpack! It’s worth more than what they’re charging for it. I looked (in person) at some 3.11 Tactical backpacks, and, this measures up in every single aspect, at a fraction of the price (for those that haven’t seen them, they’re generally well over $100). Also, the 3.11s that I looked at didn’t have padded waist straps like this one, and didn’t come with the bladder, like this one does. The padded waist straps alone up the value, plus there’s small zipper pockets on them to stash keys or whatever in...they don’t hold a plus size iPhone though. Just a smidge too small. You don’t realize how important padded waist straps can be until you’re stuck with carrying 30lbs on your back and those plain straps are digging into you, even through a heavier coat.

The padding in the back is just as good as the Swiss Army backpack I have, it’s not itchy if it gets against your skin, and it does pretty good at keeping you cool...as cool as you can be with a bag strapped to your back, at least.

There’s plenty of pockets so you can organize you’re supplies for better accessibility and it does have the nice straps on the bottom to attach a bedroll (yoga mat, if you choose) or pup tent. There’s plenty of places to add/attach other accessories and pouches. Also, the compartment for the bladder is insulated. I can’t really say how well because we haven’t tested it, but it seems it would be decent.

All around, this is just a really, really good pack, especially for the price! I fully intend on buying myself one very soon because all of my backpacks are shot (my “everyday”, and my emergency bags), and this just fit the bill...I almost kept it for myself! 😁
text_fidelity_b: Gelindo Tactical Backpack with Bladder - Insulated Military Pack with Molle System

text_fidelity_a:
Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack Suffice to say that I have a medical condition that requires me to not get too hot. Bad things happen and they are very obvious, and not in my head. I can die if I get overheated. I just have to live with it. I also live and often work outside in one of the hottest and most humid parts of the country. Oh, and I'm not rich so I can't just hire people to do my bidding and stay inside all day. The clash of these issues has caused me to try numerous gadgets to stay cool and, honestly, this one works the best (and is one of the cheapest though it could be cheaper).

Chilling vests are ridiculously expensive and marginally effective.

"Snap towels" are a joke. Don't waste your money.

You need something with ice in it, people. And the plastic ice cubes don't work, either, and here's why: real ice melts and makes your shirt cool, too, and lasts LONGER, and is cheap.

So far this towel has worked great. I've used it a dozen times or so in very harsh conditions and bought another as a backup. You buy two dollars worth of bag ice, put it in a cooler, and you have at least two days of continuous personal cooling. The towel is long enough to fit around my big neck.

My niece tried it and told her dad she's never mowing the yard again without one. My daughter has never mowed the yard so I'm still astonished about that on two levels.

So tskile it from someone whose life and vision actually depends on staying cool (I know, sounds crazy, but it is true) : if you live in a HUMID area, this is the best balance of price and cooling you can get.

I am so serious about this product I left without it on me day and drive twenty miles back to get it, then twenty miles back to where I realized I'd forgotten it. Now that's a testimony.
text_fidelity_b: Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack

text_fidelity_a:
M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch Extreme Graphite Fly Fishing Rod 4-Piece 9 Feet with IM7 Carbon Blank, Hard Chromed Guides, A Cork Grip（Size:3/4/5/6/7/8/10wt） (Extreme Rod, 9ft 4weight) Let's just say it. This is a darn nice rod. Is it a Sage? A Reddington? A Loop? Of course not. But it's also not $400.

I got this rod because I have 5wt and 6wt rods which were a bit more costly, but I wanted a 4wt for some smaller streams I'm going to be hitting. I won't spend much time there, and money is not abundant, so I figured I would try one of these. Boy was I surprised! I was expecting some moderate (slow) action rod, sloppy, and Heavy. This is light, crisp, and a joy to cast! The cork is great for this price point, and it's all put together and presented quite nicely.
There's an attitude in fly fishing that if it's not expensive, it's not worth using. Unfortunately we don't all have the ability or desire to spend $500 on a rod. For those of us in that situation, this is a magnificent option.

Look at it like this. You buy a rod at Scheels or Cabela's because you're getting a quality product at a slightly discounted price because it's store brand rather than big name brand. And that usually is the case and works well. Some of the best fishing gear I've got, and I've got a lot, was got from those brands I just named. These Maxcatch rods are built on the EXACT same blanks that the Scheel's Outfitter MDD fly rods are built on. And those were being sold for $100.

With that in mind, know that when you get one of these you aren't getting a Loomis rod. But this is probably the best sub-$120 fly rod you can get, and that leaves a lot of money for flies, tippet, line, and a reel.

I'll update this review with pics next time I go out. Buy one of these with confidence. I'll probably buy another for my wife and get a 3wt for me. I'm sold on this brand!

Lodge Cast Iron Melting Pot, Pre-Seasoned, 15-Ounce I own lots of Lodge items, but won't bore you with the merits of using cast iron - especially since I don't think a pot of this size really demonstrates all the strengths of cast iron cookware.

I purchased this little guy for 1 main reason and I have not been disappointed. I cook a lot of Indian dishes - things like dal and meat/veg curries. A common technique in Indian cooking is to heat some fat in a little pot and quickly add spices, chilies, ginger, garlic, etc. for a minute or so. Then you dump the mix into another pot which has cooked the main ingredient - things like lentils, beans, etc. The technique is called "tarka" and is an easy way to add a lot of flavor to a dish. This little pot is the perfect size for this - not too big, not too small.

I have since discovered another use for the pot. It is perfect for cooking one egg! You need very little water to poach and the small size keeps the egg compact. It's great for frying too since the egg doesn't stick to the properly seasoned cast iron.

The only problem I have with the pot is that the bottom diameter is a bit too small. I have a hard time keeping it stable on my gas burners. I fix that problem by placing a small cast iron trivet between the pot and the burner.
text_fidelity_b: Lodge Cast Iron Melting Pot, Pre-Seasoned, 15-Ounce

text_fidelity_a:
Camp Chef Everest 2 Burner Stove Update 8/21/17 - Just returned from a 5 day camping trip where I used this stove every meal and I have to drop my rating from 3 stars down to 1. Here are the reasons why I don't like this stove:
1. Extremely poor flame control. It's impossible to get and keep a low flame. If you manage to get it low enough, the slightest breeze will blow it out. Had numerous boil-overs and burnt food from the high heat.
2. No handle, or easy places to grab. This issue went from a nuisance to a real PITA the more I had to move it around.
3. No protection for the knobs/piezo lighter. They will eventually get damaged without protection.
4. Nowhere to easily hold the stove while depressing the piezo lighter with one hand. Again, a seeminly minor nuisance that turned into a real PITA - especially when the stove it hot from the left burner and trying to light the right burner.
5. No type of anti-skid on the bottom of the stove. If you're using any kind of slick surface, like a camp kitchen, it will slide all over the place especially when trying to light the burners.

I’ll jump to the bottom line first – if you’re looking for a high quality, durable camp stove that will last for decades – they don’t seem to exist anymore. Like so many of today’s products, they are manufactured to last a season or two and then replaced with the next great thing. To be fair, I’m comparing it to what it’s replacing: my 50+ year old Coleman dual fuel. But, the more I look at these new stoves, the more I think I’ll just stick with my old one. It still works great, I just wanted a new and shiny two-burner and the convenience of propane.

Here’s the highlights:

Pros
Stylish
Lightweight (can also be a con)
Size
Cleanup

Cons
Fit and finish
Shoddy workmanship
Cheap rivets
Poor temperature control on low
Plastic lid latches
Regulator
Poor two-burner flame on a small bottle
No handle

I did a lot of research and really wanted to love this stove (still do). My current camp kitchen consists of a Coleman 413E gas stove and a Coleman 5418 single burner propane stove. Little did I know that I’ve been cooking on vintage stoves for many years! I recently added a Camp Chef EX60 two burner Explorer with a large steel griddle. Yes, this was a MAJOR upgrade. It’s a beast and requires a big propane bottle. Don’t know what I was thinking, but I love it.

After the disappointment of this Camp Chef Everest, I did a lot more research and went out and actually touchy/feely’d all the other comparable stoves I could find at REI, Walmart, Target, etc. I’ll just say that I think all of these stoves, regardless of brand name, come from the same completely unsupervised and un-credentialed factory in China. There may be minor differences, but there are too many similarities to be coincidence.

So here’s the details on the Pros: It looks pretty. Sitting in your campsite it will be the envy of the campground. And when you splatter grease all over it when cooking, at least it wipes down fairly easily. It can fit a 12” and 10.5” skillet at the same time centered over the burners with the windscreens up. That’s nice. And it’s light - because it’s made out of thin stamped metal and lightweight pop-rivets.

Now for the Cons. I figured almost nothing else mattered if it performed. But it doesn’t, and so everything else does matter. Ask yourself why you think you need a “high output/high BTU” stove. Presumably to boil water faster. It’s certainly not for cooking because you’ll never use high output for regular cooking. And high output does not equate to better performance. I’ll bet there are 11,000 BTU burners that will boil water just as fast as these. Frankly, these burners just don’t perform very well at low, medium, or high settings. At the very lowest setting there is a huge yellow flame that just won’t go away. Same on high. Only somewhere in the middle do you find a sweet spot for the flame, but it’s too hot for normal cooking. With two burners going, the small propane bottle just can’t keep up and both flames become unmanageable. I didn’t try using the bigger bottle lacking a hose. Which brings me to the regulator. It’s garbage, I don’t trust it, and I’m sure it will fail in short order. Both of the points where the tube joins the connectors shows very poor quality control. Not to mention it’s crooked when hooked up to the stove – meaning the connector part of the stove is not centered in the hole.

All of the bad reviews you read about poor fit and finish are true. There are sharp edges where the drip pan meets the body. The wind screens don’t line up without actually bending the pieces to achieve a “custom fit”, but that’s easy because the metal is flimsy and they used cheap pop-rivets which insures everything is loosely attached. The hinges that attach the top to the bottom are a joke – stamped aluminum and poorly attached with pop-rivets. There is no way the plastic lid latches are going to last – I’m surprised they survived shipping. I can’t stress enough how un-durable this stove is. But, it’s exactly the same as all the others.

To test out the cooking ability, I’ve cooked 3 things: pan roasted potatoes, pan roasted cross-cut ribs – both in cast iron skillets, and scrambled eggs in a non-stick pan. All 3 of these require good temperature control at low to medium-low setting. Note: I can do all of these perfectly on my Coleman 513E. On the lowest setting, my potatoes were over-crisped before cooking completely through. The cross-cut ribs probably would have been ok, but I missed the sweet spot for a second and they over-cooked. The scrambled eggs actually turned out ok, but I was very careful and moved the pan on and off the flame as needed while cooking. All in all, I think you can turn out good food on this stove, but for me it’s going to take way too much attention and fussing. I think I want something with lower BTU burners that perform and adjust better.
text_fidelity_b: Camp Chef Everest 2 Burner Stove

text_fidelity_a:
YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments My wife and I prefer weights as a workout, but both of us find the handles our community provides for the lat pull to be uncomfortable. The community provides the bar and nylon strap options, but 1. even with leather gloves they are uncomfortable, and 2. as a shorter guy my arm span is not such that I can get and maintain a comfortable reach (I can't hold the rubber grips on the bar), so for safety and comfort, I'm outta luck. But when I saw this YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for the gym I thought it might help me with comfort and safety, and be something she and I could both use to help improve.

The YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment is as easy as any attachment for the lat pull to get on and off, fitting the community's machine easily. There is a concern we have, but only time will tell if it plays out: the connection has a plastic exterior over what appears to be a metal disk, but we cannot tell how far that metal extends. It SEEMS as though it is only a disk and that the majority of the top piece is plastic. So we are not sure for how long or how much weight this connector will last. It is not that we have "proof" of it being subpar, just concerning by appearance.

The material of the rope itself also seems, not as overall strong, but as we are not at all experts in these materials or what is common in most of the heavy work gyms, we have nothing to compare it to. So we are going with it being an appropriate set up and provided materials. For our level of weights, even as I get stronger, we don't see it being at all an issue.

Lastly is the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment's handgrip, where you get that ergonomic element. I attempt to show in the various images how it is structured, curveted for the hand to rest within, allowing for a strong and comfortable grip. Again, I'm a shorter guy, so I also have a smaller hand. My wife's fingers are slightly longer than mine. We each find that the grip is both good and bad. We can each grip it and feel we have a secure hold. We feel safe. We feel a great pull. However, we each have a spot on the grip where it cuts into our finger/hand and begins to rub. In two images I show 1. the grip itself as I hold it up, then 2. my thumb over the top - it is at this point for me where it rubs and begins to feel like it's cutting into the thumb. Again, it is my hand size. My wife's issue is in the palm. She can fully and comfortably grip the handle, but at the base of the palm there is a cutting pressure.

So, do we like the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment? Yes, very much.
In spite of the issue and admittedly, with only using it twice for our full reps, we do like it. I will add, we have not worn our gloves during these workouts. We normally do, but circumstances had us in there without them, so using our bare hands, we did come up with discomfort whereby we got through the workouts, but didn't go full out as the discomfort grew. BUT, we both feel like once we have on the leather gloves the issue will at the least decrease greatly enough so as to allow us a full on workout and be okay. I will update if that does not pan out. But for each of us, the better grip and the overall feel of the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment as far as what we can do, how safe we feel, and even comfort to the greater part of our hands is enough. We went with the 4 star because of the issue, but WE THINK THAT if they were to add a more comfortable cushion (rubber, something) to the grip, this would be a great 5 star grip.
text_fidelity_b: YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments

text_fidelity_a:
Suntour SR SP12 Suspension seat Post UPDATE: I weight 210 lbs. and the stock soft spring works great on pavement. In fact it works better on pavement than the hard, red spring intended for riders over 180lbs. It works better on pavement even with the preload set at zero (loosest). The optional hard, red spring is intended only for riders over 180lbs WHO ARE RIDING OFF-ROAD. Trust me. I purchased both. The good new is it is easy to change out springs in well under 5 minutes.

ORIGINAL: Be careful when ordering because the product page defaults to the 27.2mm diameter. How this is less expensive from the UK with free shipping and free returns is a mystery. Strangely, the optional hard (red) spring for riders over 180lbs does not seem to be anywhere on Amazon. I had to order it directly from Suntour.

The optional hard red spring is different than the 31.6 stock spring. The stock spring has a cast inner portion the fills the 31.6 inner diameter giving the spring greater stability. The manual states that the hard, (red) PKE100-20 spring (the only hard red spring on Suntour's website) is intended only for the 27.2mm post, that a hard PKE100-21 or -23 is required for the 31.6mm. Yet Suntour's website states the PKE100-20 is 'Compatible with all sizes of SR Suntour seat post.' I guess they found that the PKE100-20 could do the job on the 31.6 and they could phase out the -21 and -23. It works so I'm not going to worry about it unless something goes wrong.

The preload adjustment is not adequately explained anywhere. I adjusted it by trial and error. When I remove the spring for maintenance I will measure the depth of the threaded cap so I can duplicate my preload adjustment during reassembly.

There's a no-name brand at about this same price with only 20mm of travel so this is a good value with 50mm. Some more expensive brands have 90mm of travel which seems unnecessary because I weigh 210lbs and this one has never yet bottomed out on asphalt. I haven't yet tested it off road. Plus the one with 90mm needs close to six inches of exposed seat post. I have tall frames so the 90mm couldn't work for me anyway.

Even the bumps on asphalt were taking their toll on my aging bones but this fixed it. A very good and robust product.
text_fidelity_b: Suntour SR SP12 Suspension seat Post

The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle - Incl. Balance Trainer for All Sports, Gym, Standing Desk, or Yard Games, 2x Fitness Balls, Ball Pump and more First, I have to admit, we only used this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle once since arriving. It arrived at the same point my wife and I got sick (we’ve been down for a few weeks), so it’s been in the corner since unpacking and had only one test run. My pics would normally be of the product fully unwrapped and ready for use and/or in use.

But in these pictures you see the size of the bundle included. Pictures of the set show the number of pieces including the two balls, the cushion, and the board (dark brown flat item), and thickness of the board. “Out of the box,” if you will, this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle is a great deal with multiple pieces offering an athlete or anyone working out several options - the cushion is about our speed for beginning, but I know with the balls you can make it harder or easier based on how big the ball is you choose to use, or how much you fill it. The number of items included in the bundle alone makes it a great deal in our book. We have had a previous, similar workout board that only included the board and cushion (to be fair, it was half the price), but while we truly enjoyed that set, we were unable to move up if we wanted without buying more. So that you get as much here as you do is a plus.

We only unwrapped the cushion and platform for our initial test run, and found them both to be excellent for our needs. The thickness of the board made us both comfortable and with a listed weight up to 300 lbs., even with the extra weight I’m working off I am safe and comfortable on the board. We found the cushion to be easy to get inflated and hold the air. Having had one before we knew how to use it and were quickly getting on and off and balancing. We always use ours for both standing on and as a platform for planking and like the challenge. We have not (as of yet) put the non-skid surface on (again, we’ve been down), but have not decided either way if we’ll use it, but we have it for when we are ready.

We are also looking forward to trying the two balls. At this point neither of us is comfortable yet to try, so we’re unable to speak to it, but we love that this is an option to move into once we are ready. In the end we are very pleased with the bundle and feel this The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board will help us get back up and going once we are recovered. Just that test run reminded us how much we love this kind of core workout and how well it worked for us in the past. We’re happy to be able to do this again and believe the The Skill Board Mini Beginner to Pro - Wooden Balance Board for Adults Bundle will be great moving forward.

text_fidelity_a: iDOO Inflatable Couch, Blow Up Sofa 3 Seater with Built-in Pump, Camping Inflatable Chair, Portable Air Couch with Backrest, Blow Up Lounger, 3-Min Fast Inflation Deflation, Easy to Storage This sturdy little air-couch is little different than their bed and by that I mean, well-made and can take the weight but still stay fully inflated.  What I really like about this couch is that, like my IDOO queen size bed, it has an internal air compressor so you don't have to purchase an air compressor (or find that one you have for inflating pool toys).  The cord, once the couch is inflated, folds completely away and the very best part is that this couch can be inflated (and deflated) within 2-3 minutes!  My queen size bed can be fully inflated/deflated within 5 minutes.  That's helpful should you find several surprise guests show up at your house - grab this couch, plug it in and 5 minutes later you and your guests are enjoying a wonderful if unexpected visit in comfort!  Okay, so there is one downside and that is an air couch (and my air mattress) are so lightweight that they can rock forward when trying to stand up.  I have a large rug under my mattress to combat that rolling/moving motion when standing up.  It works more or less, but this couch's width works against it.  I don't know if maybe having a couple of weighted bags that attach to the back/bottom of this couch with velcro strips might work or not, but it's a thought I may try.  Again, for the ease of storing (in its own bag in a closet), ease of inflation/deflation, and being completely self-contained (with its own air compressor), this is a wonderful instant seating option for me and probably many others.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count First impressions.
1) The Inspire watch came with about a 14% charge which was insufficient for the required firmware update. It came with a large band and a small band. I have a small wrist but the small band looked child-size. I purchased a set of clips for the Inspire for when I want to clip it to my pants rather than use it as a watch.
2) The Inspire charged to 100% in about 90 minutes.
3) I used an Inspire Charger Dock which I'm very glad I purchased after reading reviews. It has a long USB cable, magnetically clicks to the Inspire and makes charging very easy.
4) The watch was at 92% after the required firmware update via the Fitbit app.
5) Today, after less than 24% the watch is already at 82%. There were a lot of reviews about how quickly the Inspire loses battery charge. I have 'all day sync' and 'always connected' turned off and only synced with the app three times today, but it still lost 10% of the charge.
6) I had some problems connecting the Inspire to the Fitbit app. I tried about 6 times before the app connected. I kept getting a Fitbit maintenance error. The app then took about an hour to update the firmware on the Inspire. I did have to reboot my phone before the Inspire successfully paired with the app.
7) Since pairing the Inspire quickly synced each time I opened the app.

I'll update my review after trying out out for a few weeks.

NOTE: The Inspire can be returned to Amazon within 45 days and has a limited 1 year warranty with support via Fitbit customer service (2 year warranty if purchased in the EEU). You will receive an offer in the app to extend the warranty to 2 years. I didn't personally feel like spending an additional 24.99 for an extended warranty. If the Inspire fails after a year I'll purchase a different brand.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Nite Ize See 'Em Mini LED Bicycle Spoke Lights, Wheel Lights for Nighttime Visibility + Safety, 2 Pack, Blue I got these to use in place of the larger/bulkier Nite Ize Spoke Lit wheel lights (the rubberized ones that snap on to a spoke), and have been satisfied so far. I'm using these on 2 bikes, and have attached them to traditional round-spoke wheels as well as wheels with flat/"bladed" spokes, and they fit both and stay on (haven't had one fly off yet). These use different (smaller, CR927) batteries than some other Nite Ize lights, and I haven't used them enough to rate battery life yet. I got these mainly because the Spoke Lit model had a habit of getting loose and banging against the fork.

Good Stuff:
-smaller than other spoke lights; haven't had problems with them rubbing the fork, brakes, etc. on mountain or road bike
-seem to stay in-place a bit better than the Spoke Lit model (at least one they're positioned correctly); these fasten with a clip instead of just a press-fit
-lighter than the older Spoke Lit model

Bad Stuff:
-not as bright; will be visible, but if you want a lot of wattage on the wheel, may need to double-up
-only light the wheel in one direction; thus, a pack of 2 would cover 1 wheel
-no blink mode; just solid-on or solid-off
text_fidelity_b: Nite Ize See 'Em Mini LED Bicycle Spoke Lights, Wheel Lights for Nighttime Visibility + Safety, 2 Pack, Blue

SUUNTO Movestick Mini (Black, One Size) worked with my Garmin 310XT on my Mac Pro without having to install anything. I already had the Garmin ANT+ stick installed and was using that, I simply took that out of the USB slot and put this in. I though I'd have to install something but after awhile the Garmin started syncing to it. Love that it worked right away. Although some times after a workout it takes a bit longer for it to recognize and connect automatically to my Garmin 310xt and start the data transfer. Usually I just leave the ANT+ stick in my Mac and synch my workouts after I'm done. However on a recent out of town trip I had forgotten to pack the ANT+ stick so I needed a replacement. I had read that this works just as well as the Garmin (some reviewers say even better) so at a significantly lower price and smaller size than the Garmin stick, I decided to give this a try so that I could keep it with my MacBook Pro that I use when traveling. I am very pleased with it and it is definitely worth it for the better price and works just as well as the Garmin stick, except for the occasional times when it doesn't seem to find the Garmin. When that happens I've just pulled it out and put it back in the USB slot and it usually finds the Garmin and starts transferring the data.

In Summary:

Pros:
+ Works great with Mac OSX - just plug it in!
+ cheaper than the Garmin ANT+ stick
+ small form factor - so no worry about accidentally bumping it against it and knocking it out of the USB slot during data transfer

Cons:
+ Some times takes a while to recognize my Garmin 310xt
+ small form factor - could get lost easily - but this is not really an issue to me, though may be for some folks so thought I'd mention it.

Conclusion: If it didnt' have that occasional little blip of not connecting, I'd give it 5 stars. Still I'm very pleased with it and would definitely recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: SUUNTO Movestick Mini (Black, One Size)

text_fidelity_a:
IRON COMPANY Body-Solid Leverage Squat/Calf Machine Let me start by saying I have been lifting in gyms for about 30 years and even qualified for Nationals as bodybuilder when I was 27....I'm 43 now. Still going at it strong but wanted a home calf raise machine and an alternative to barbell squats. I've probably lifted on just about any and all commercial grade equipment out there. Here are my thoughts on this piece of equipment and why I only gave it 3 stars. I hope it helps.

1) As others have stated...there are no directions and let's be serious...how irritating is that? If you can't bother giving your customer assembly instructions how much can you really honestly care about your customer? Just my two cents.

2) The contents are ill packaged and yes, I understand that Fed Ex shakes the boxes. But both boxes looked like they were packaged by a 5 year old. Just a total mess...screws...bolts...washer...thrown around in the box with shredded styrofoam and broken tight downs. I can't possibly see how any shipper could have created this total mess. Again, extreme sloppiness leads me to believe there is a lack of concern for the person receiving it.

3) 50% of the reason I purchased this piece of equipment was for the standing calf raise, my local gym only has the seated calf raise. I've had this exact same piece of equipment before by PowerTec....and I wasn't sure how I was going to feel about the rounded calf raise platform versus the flat one that power tec made and every other commercial grade piece of gym equipment uses. Now I know why they don't use a rounded platform. U have less contact material with your foot when you raise up. Is it the end of the world? No...but I'm just not a huge fan of the rounded platform. I much more prefer the standard flat platform that feels natural and more comfortable on the feet.

4) The step up from floor level to the calf raise machine is a bit hairy once you get some heavy weight on the machine...3 to 4...45's on each side. I wish the platform was designed differently so all that weight is not stacked onto on leg and your back is torqued when you step up. Commercial grade equipment is made in such a way that the platform is directly under you....you start on the calf platform...you don't load the weight and then step up. This machine is set up so that in order to have the weight directly on your shoulders...where it needs to be....you are standing one step behind the calf platform. Then in order to do the calf raise...you have to step up onto the platform...one leg at at time with all the weight on your back and one leg down...and one leg taking a step. Not good in my opinion.

5) The angle of the squat. Ahh...its okay....makes you feel like you are doing a deep squat but in reality even a deep squat on this machine is not even a parallel squat. If you have someone else do a deep squat and watch their lower leg in relation to their upper...you will see that the deepest squat on this machine is still a high squat in reality. Your leg is simply at a different angle and gives the false sense that you are performing a deep squat...when in fact you are not.

Will this take the place of a regular squat?

Yes, and No.

If you are a gym rat and you perform squats correctly than this piece of equipment will never take the place of or produce the same results.

If you are like 95% of the guys in the gym that never ever reach parallel when they squat because they were too busy stacking on the weight instead of learning good form at the beginning...than yes...this piece of equipment will keep you squatting a bit high and allow you to keep stacking the weight on and the ego flying high.

Can you get a good calf workout on this machine?

Absolutely. Even with the rounded platform that I do not like...you can still get a great calf workout.

Would I buy it again?

I'm on the fence with this one. I wouldn't cry if it was removed from my home...but I wouldn't send it back either.

I use the squat portion in addition to my leg workout....not as my primary piece of equipment...and I think that is what it is good for...and addition to regular squats....leg press...lungs...extensions...curls...etc. etc.

Hope my review helped somone.
text_fidelity_b: IRON COMPANY Body-Solid Leverage Squat/Calf Machine

I did read the item description that said they fit up to 43mm, but I took a chance that they would fit on my 44mm rifle scopes objective lenses.  These are cushioned spring clips.  They are NOT super heavy duty, but they are functional.  They do fit onto a 44mm objective lens.  They could easily be knocked off in the brush, should you have to run thru any.  They do what they are supposed to do, tho.  I shined a flashlight into the unit, and I got no flashback, so I'd say it's good in sunlight.  I also intend to take a small but stout rubber band and put the rubber band over the clamps to help keep the kill flash clamps more snug onto the front of the scope objective lens.  I say again, these will come off if scraped or rubbed very hard against something.  I do believe the best flash killers are the ones that thread directly inside of the objective lenses that have internal threads.  Those options are also a lot more money.  So for the money and function, these flash killers get 5 stars for now.  If they happen to fall off under heavy recoil (I shoot 308 and 30-06), I will change my rating.

text_fidelity_a:
Atpylan Large Capacity Lunch Bag for Women Men, Reusable Cooler Bag Collapsible Coolers for Travel I call this a tote rather than a cooler because it does more than a cooler does. In fact, I'll be using it mostly to transport warm items than I will cold.

PROs
- I love the dark blue color(C2-blue). I saw a photo on a different review and it looked like a brighter blue. Unless there was a different color offered that I'm unaware of, the dark blue is true to color on the listing.
- This will hold quite a bit. If you're like me and plan on using it to bring food items to potlucks, this will do well.
- The top pocket (also insulated) can hold any utensils, spices, napkins, or other items you may want to bring along. Or more ice packs, if using it as a cooler.
- There's an additional front (insulated) pocket and two side mesh pockets for whatever your heart desires. Pockets galore.
- It's collapsible.
- There are two handles that meet in the center and can be held together with a short hook and loop sleeve. That makes it so convenient, particularly if you're carrying heavier items. The handles aren't digging into your hands then. Instead there's a sleeve adding comfort.
- There is an optional shoulder strap, however, see the cons below for further detail...

CONs
- The optional shoulder strap is nice to have, however, the point of weight bearing lies upon two plastic hooks on each side. I've included a photo of one of them. I don't believe I would trust those when carrying heavier loads.
- The bottom of the bag does not have a hard surface. I will likely find something I can put on the bottom to make it firm when carrying items of different sizes, etc. Perhaps I'll double up on some cardboard and wrap it in foil or something. I'm not sure yet.

All in all I love this bag and would definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Atpylan Large Capacity Lunch Bag for Women Men, Reusable Cooler Bag Collapsible Coolers for Travel

It is a short, stubby, relatively heavy .45 acp semi auto pistol available in stainless steel.. While it won't win any beauty contests, it has a presence all its own and the intimidation factor it provides is awesome. It's the kind of weapon that when you run out of ammo you can hit your opponent in the face with it for the game winner.

This ZT 0456 has that kind of look to it. It has some (short and stubby) curves but the overall construction is what draws attention to itself. Yes, it is a bit on the (slightly) heavy side, but this knife wasn't designed to be slim and beautiful. It is designed to work, and work hard, taking on any task from cutting to prying that you come up against. How many knives do you have in your collection that can be carried in your pocket, can dispatch any simple cutting jobs with aplomb, and then allow you to pry open a door with it. Most EDC blades don't have the spine for it, much less the overall design and build that would allow even attempting that task.

As I have aged I have learned that a knife should be much more than just a cutting tool. None of my automatic knives can even approach the type of hard work that this Zero Tolerance knife can conquer. The blade is sharp but heavy, the locking mechanism is tight and solid, and the flipper works like butter. People notice it when I pull it from my pocket, not just because it's a knife but because of the attractive and unique design. Everyone wants to know what it is, how much it costs, and where can they "legally" get one. This is one of those places.

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor Round TWO! I'd bought this identical HRM kit back in February 2014. From day one, I'd get WILDLY erratic readings on the heart rate - but that's ok, cuz I am actually from Planet Mars. No machine in any gym, nor any kind of heart rate monitor on Planet Earth works consistently on me. I either get zero reading (when my Martian paws are on the piece of exercise equipment) or I get rates that jump from 189 to 60 to 132, and so on. Don't tell the NSA, because I'm here on a secret mission: to see if my second purchase of this Polar FT60 HRM works. I should've registered my initial purchase back in Feb, but being a foolish optimist, I used the HRM daily - till it plain died on me long about August. I stopped getting any kind of reading between the transmitter and the device - even after new batteries were inserted. So I assumed it was a goner.

What I LOVE about this HRM:
- It gives me the data I need to stick with my fitness program: how many minutes spent in zone 1, 2, & 3 (based on initial VO2 reading and the 6-min fitness test I took first time I took it to the gym); my total calories burned and what percentage of them were fat; my average and max heart rate (which, on the first device I purchased gave the "accurately" bizarre ranges of 189 to 62, but I know why that is). That is ALL I need to know. I'm not a marathon runner or even daily runner. My goal is to burn 400+ calories in a variety of ways at the gym (or outdoors) on most days of the week. I don't need to know my footfall, cadence, how much foot is on the ground every nano-second, my GPS coordinate, or about 100 other functions that other HRMs provide (and which are no doubt of interest to the athlete wearing them).
- It's easy to find your VO2 (well, maybe it's based on a lame algorithm, but I have SOME number to work with)
- It's compatible with ALL the machines in my gym, so I don't have to keep looking down at my wrist every few seconds (like I did with the Garmin) to see what my heart rate is - a BIG plus!
- It's pretty intuitive to operate, once you spend 5 min learning the main buttons.
- It's a good-looking watch
- It doesn't drain the battery like some of the Garmin devices (unless you shut off GPS and turn the device off)

What I HATE about the device (Product Development: READ ME FIRST)
- the buttons are CRIPPLINGLY PAINFUL to press. It's ridiculous, but no kidding, I had to press the dang buttons against a flat, hard piece of granite counter to actually get them to depress.
- OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! OUCH! I have short nails, but they'd just slip off the button if I used them, so I use the fleshy tip of my now CRIPPLED, broken finger to press the idiotically STIFF buttons on this watch. I mean come ON: spend a nickel more and get some decent springs under these buttons, so I don't get arthritis from pressing them every day.
- These painful buttons drove me to THROW the whole kit away when it stopped working (my duh) and go buy a Garmin HRM right here at Amazon.com. Unfortunately, that device seems to require a PhD in Rocket Science to call up the right screens to find the few bits of data I was interested in. PLUS that device also gave very erratic readings, given that it was not made for a Martian, but rather an Earthling.
- I think that for the money paid, the Polar FT60 should *in theory* last longer than a scant 6 mos? The warranty is for 2 years, but I've read elsewhere (mostly from a few years back) that other folks complained about their device conking out.

I'm going to register this HRM and take good care of it, cuz despite the NUMBINGLY PAINFUL buttons, it is the only device that gives me the exact data I want to see after each workout.

Please Polar: Make these buttons easier to press, huh?
text_fidelity_b: POLAR FT60 Heart Rate Monitor

That type of climate, which is subtropical, is perfect for bugs. And boy, do we have them. I looked at a few hats with mosquito netting added to it but realized that I couldn't get the total head and neck coverage I needed for proper UPF sun protection.

Since I just had a melanoma removed from my back (with surgery including 56 stitches), I'm very careful about what I wear in the sun when working on our landscaping. I couldn't find beekeepers' hats which provided both UPF 50 in the hat as well as side and back flaps to protect my neck. So I quickly realized that the solution was to buy the netting separate and simply use it over the proper sun protection hats that I already had.

I ordered this triple pack of mosquito head netting for a number of reasons. They are economical, well-built, are loose fitting, are a very neutral khaki color, and have a very tight mesh to protect against the tiniest buggers. The khaki color does not absorb heat from the sun and is easy to see through. Since our Florida yellow flies are attracted to dark colors, khaki is the way to go.

text_fidelity_a: Real Relax Under Desk Treadmill, Portable, Slim Walking Pad Space Saving Motorized Treadmill for Home Office Workout, No Installation Required Okay, so I'm near the upper limit of the treadmill's rated weight support.  I got this as a way to get myself walking regularly.  Understand that I live in Texas and until this week when we had 24 hours of rain that resulted in 10 inches of rain - nearly as much as we were down for 3 months...before that we had I believe 67 days in a row of 100+ degree days with even the night temps barely dipping below 90.  Skinny people may be okay walking in that heat, but not a fat person trying to lose weight!  So, for me, I have been walking slow and in short "bursts" to get acclimated and able to move up in speed and time.  T had been wanting an easy treadmill to store as I live in a small house - a mobile home which is the early version of a tiny house, before tiny homes were a "thing."  Anyway, I have this in my bedroom stashed behind a chair next to my bed.  It is easy to pull out and step on to begin my walk.  At the moment, I am walking about 15 minutes at a time.  My goal is to get to 1 hour and then I can begin walking faster to get some cardio involved with the walk.  I have also incorporated yoga so that I am working on muscle strength as well.  This treadmill is helping, but I was afraid, when I got it, that it wouldn't work well for me because I was a bit too heavy for it.  That's why I would ask that the people who make this should look into making it sturdier for those of us who are trying to improve our heath by using a treadmill.  Make it handle 300 or maybe up to 350 pounds would make it helpful for those who want to take charge of their weight loss at home.
text_fidelity_b: Real Relax Under Desk Treadmill, Portable, Slim Walking Pad Space Saving Motorized Treadmill for Home Office Workout, No Installation Required

That's okay. I am accustomed to this. I can service my own hub/axle. But the builder painted the axles making it near impossible to open the hub to grease and adjust the cones.

I tried a 16mm socket on one end of the axle for leverage and adjustable crescent on the other. Slow going. Then a high-quality needle-nosed vice-grip on the crescent side. Still no love.

Now I'm reduced to overnight soaking in PB-Blaster to try to dissolve the paint. Next? Paint remover?

This is just too much work for a component valued at very close to $100.

text_fidelity_a:
Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair - The Starter - Back Support Folding Seat for Meditation, Yoga Floor Chair(White/Navy Blue) I grabbed this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair with a thought towards our days at the beach. Sometimes we have chairs, sometimes just the towels, but I thought this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair might offer me a nice, supportive place to sit. My wife tends to lay out for sun, but I like watching the water and thinking... but I can get tired and start to hurt on the hard sand. This is smaller and easier to carry overall (I thought), so why not. In the end, I think I’m going to be correct in my assessment. We’re not getting back out there (yet), but the time is soon upon us for our beach days and I can’t wait.

The Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair is a cool idea - a stadium seat type set up: flips open, cushion, back support. I’ve tried one or two such seats and thought, eh. But we don’t do stadiums enough. We do, however, sit on the floor from time to time, go to the beach, mediate, and so forth. Hitting that “middle age” timeframe, my wife and I would love to have something more comfortable.

1. I gave it 5 stars because overall it feels like that’s right for comfort, ease of use, and so forth. I would consider a 4 star for the magnets that hold the seat to the frame. I’ve had the seat cushions pop off every time I’ve picked it up to carry/move, or take pictures. My wife has not as such luck, only having them fall a couple time. Closed they’d slide up coming off for me, so I’d be worried about loosing one or two or all three - though I’m sure one would notice that many.

2. The cushions are nice for comfort. It comes with three, with one having a strap on the back to hold it onto the other - so you can have a double seat cushion, which is a nice add on.

3. Seems to hold a good amount of weight. I’ve got some extra pounds on right now and it seems to handle me well. I’m taking it off, so hoping it won’t be there all summer as I plan to use it, but so far, so good.

4. The frame seems solid and like it’ll hold up. Again, it holds our weight (individually) and allows us to feel well supported. My wife has tried it more, sitting both cross legged and straight and feels like she can sit there for a good amount of time in both positions.

5. The seat cushions are good - not too thick (though thicker is always better), but not too thin. They were comfortable on both the back and seat.

6. This Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair comes with a strap that you can remove, attaching to the base of the frame allowing you to carry it over the shoulder. My wife did this and felt like both the strap was comfortable, while the chair was not too heavy. We both agree this is a solid, with a noticeable weight to it, but nothing most folks couldn’t handle (we think), finding the strap to be a good addition to aiding that. This is where you’ll want to be aware of the magnets not necessarily holding the seat in place - at least one popped off each time I tried, but only once for my wife. Because of how it sets when you are carrying on the strap - with the open side downward - it would allow the cushion to slip out onto the ground. I grabbed it before it did, but one needs to be aware, so as not to loose any. We talked about adding a strap of our own (sort of a bungie type thing) to hold the cushions in place. But that could be used for other things as well - we just don’t know what that is at this point.

7. Back support - we have only used it on the bed (that was not working too well as we’d fall over, but it was fun trying) and floor in the living room. But the back support was solid and let us feel comfortable. We both felt like it would be a nice support and keep us from hunching over and getting sore quickly.

In the end we are both impressed with this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair and plan to get some solid use out of it. I think this will be one item where time will tell - does it hold up, does it allow for longer periods of sitting, does it take different surfaces (beach, floor, grass, etc)? We’re happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair - The Starter - Back Support Folding Seat for Meditation, Yoga Floor Chair(White/Navy Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
JOOLA Tour Elite Pickleball Bag – Backpack & Duffle Bag for Paddles & Pickleball Accessories – Thermal Insulated Pockets Hold 4+ Paddles - With Fence This JOOLA pickle ball bag offers cool (bright) colors, is well designed and constructed, and will allow you to bring along all the gear you want and need. I got this for my wife and she loves it. We are admittedly beginners in the world of pickle ball, but we already know that having the right gear, ready at your fingertips is the best way to enjoy your game. We both think this JOOLA bag offers just that.

The colors here are bright and bold (like my wife) and easily seen from a distance. Does this matter? Probably not, but she loves it. And as she does with her purses, feels that brighter colors on the inside helps her spot things deep within a bag (I have to agree). The materials look and feel top notch, like they'll last a good long time and take what you throw at them. The zippers are good quality and move easily, without sticking or hooking. The mesh inside is excellent as is all the different types of materials they chose to include here. Everything looks and feels like it's going to last. Putting it all together, the construction matches, meaning you can use this JOOLA bag with confidence.

There are a great number of pockets and spots for your various game gear as well as personal needs. (we were still finding a couple later in the day). For example: each side has three matching spots including the silver temperature lined slot for your paddles. We are not sure how or why, but as it appears to be the same materials found in picnic bags and baskets, so we are guessing this keeps them cool, perhaps from warping (?), and separate from other items. There is room for at least one on each side (we did not test more than one). The black inside pouch is a nice material that could hold a wallet, keys, that kind of thing. Or the yellow-blue one also with smaller items. At the end is the (now obligatory) shoe space. It is cavernous and ready to take most any size shoe. Remember, this will also take up room inside, but this bag is sure to give you plenty of room even with those size 13s. There are inside pockets as well, for separating any number of items behind both mesh and solid material. There is even the keys hook to keep them from getting lost. All pretty standard these days, but in this JOOLA bag you're going to find things spacious and easy to use. It also offers both a handle and backpack option - we try to show the thickness of the backpack handles in a couple pictures - making for an easy and comfortable way to carry your gear. And don't forget the hook pocket - behind the zipper on the back of the bag - where the hook is large and hard plastic and should do well hanging this JOOLA bag for easy access or storage. There is also this REALLY long, deep pocket back there... we are still trying to figure out what goes in it, though umbrella came to mind. Note the picture with my arm inside...

Overall we love this JOOLA pickle ball bag and my wife cannot wait for our next game. It has every space we can think of wanting, from shoes to gear to extra clothes and even a towel. And that long pocket... But the bottomline is, this is a quality bag you'll be proud to carry and find great for ease of use, amount of space provided, and all the places you can think of to carry and store your pickle ball needs. We're thrilled to have it.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Tour Elite Pickleball Bag – Backpack & Duffle Bag for Paddles & Pickleball Accessories – Thermal Insulated Pockets Hold 4+ Paddles - With Fence

text_fidelity_a:
Horizon Fitness T101-04 (Old Model) Like so many of you who reviewed this treadmill, I did my research. It took a while but I finally settled on the Horizon T101-04. It got great reviews everywhere I looked.
My treadmill arrived on time and undamaged. I asked the driver to take it down a slight grassy hill and around thru my back door and he did. I was concerned about damage because so many reviewers had problems with broken parts. I have some blemishes on the arms of the treadmill and a tiny crack on the arm of the console but other than that, it's in perfect condition.
My friend Tom (with me "helping") put it together in about 40 minutes - from box to completion. No problem with assembly and the instructions were straight forward. There weren't a lot of parts so that was a good thing. I liked that all the screws were in little plastic bags and marked as to which ones to use first. The tools needed to assemble the treadmill were included except for a screwdriver. We did not lube the belt prior to use.
Everything worked as soon as I plugged it in. Yes, the warning beeps are LOUD but I live alone so only the dog is startled when I turn the treadmill on.
This is a good solid machine. I did my first 3 miles on it yesterday and nothing moved except me. No squeaks either. I am 5'8" and 147 lbs. My long stride presented no problems. And, this treadmill is very quiet. It has 2 cup holders and I use one to hold the TV remote. Ironically, I watched "CHOPPED" while I did my work out. The fan is not very powerful, neither are the speakers but I don't care about that. I liked that you can program your workout and I am doing 18 minute miles. You can also increase or decrease the speed as you go along and the incline is great.

The mat is thick and my knees don't hurt anymore as with some 1/4 inches thick mats. But the density of the mat material is not high. It is a bit too soft, too stretchy, and too slippery (between the mat and floor). It is so soft that sometimes it turns into a "J" or "C" shape when I am doing postures on it. When I feet are wide apart on the mat, I can see that the part of the mat between my feet is stretching and the distance between my feet is becoming larger without my moving the feet. This is a bit scary because if the mat rips between my feet I can fall miserably and badly hurt myself.

Today, my yoga teacher saw my mat moving while doing postures on it. She suggested that I better stand on the floor!

The pros:
1. Soft and good cushion.
2. Inexpensive for a 1/2 inches thick mat ($19.99).
3. Black Mountain Products gives a free mat bag.

The cons:
1. Smaller than the size given in product description.
2. Too soft and stretchy due to the low density of the material.
3. Slippery on most floor surfaces.
4. No lighter color options.
text_fidelity_b: Black Mountain Products Yoga and Exercise Mat, 1/2 x 73 1/2 x 24 1/2-Inch

text_fidelity_a:
iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat My daughter and I love this seat. I bought it because I did not want to haul a heavy trailer.

It is installed on my beach cruiser and it fits perfectly - plenty of room for me to reach the handlebars and pedal without the bike seat in the way. I am 5'4" short. It was easy to install. I am surprised at how stable and natural it feels.

I bought it when she was 10 months old, but she was too small to use it. I started using it when she was just over 1 yr and she fit much better (she is average size).

So far we do short rides around the neighborhood in the evenings and weekends and I can take her 1.5 miles to daycare, and she loves it. She can also look up and see me and ring the bell. We can talk about the things we see on the ride, unlike if we had a trailer.

She has fallen asleep twice while riding. There is nowhere for her head to go, but to slump sideways. I have just supported her head with my hand for the few minutes it takes me to get home.

One very nice aspect to this seat is that it mounts on the bike stem, so when she grabs the handlebars, she can't get any torque to steer the bike.

Mine came with the padding for the seat.

Cons:
The shoulder straps are a little strange - they can slide off her shoulder, but this won't be a problem when she is bigger.

The bar that comes down over the child's lap has a cheap attachment mechanism. This ought to be fixed in the next models - it is not acceptable for a product this expensive.

In a light rain (like we encountered last weekend), water puddles in the bottom of the foot cups - I might drill a hole on the bottom of each one (we live in the Pacific NorthWest).
text_fidelity_b: iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat

text_fidelity_a:
Marcy Folding Motorized Treadmill/Electric Running Machine - Easy Assembly JX-650W So this is a rather nice basic treadmill (well by today's standards), that comes in a relatively compact (like fits in a minivan compact) box that's crazy heavy. Mine arrived in good shape, though the box had some battle scars and FedEx kinda locked us in by pupping the box so the door wouldn't open. The console and electronics would have been top notch 10-15 years ago, but it's not some web connected device with monthly subscriptions to live trainers ... then again, you don't pay for all that either. When not in use, it folds up, and gives you space for stretching or whatever.

The running platform is comfy, wide, and able to handle longer sessions. It could use better handrails (they're small, yet always in the way--I guess it helps you keep your form), and treadmills that cost twice the price are better made... then again, this isn't twice the price. The belt stays firm up to 6mph, where it starts to slip. That's enough for a walk, jog, and some running. At 7mph the belt starts to slip forward (only slightly) with each landing. Serious runners (and arm swingers--those handles can hurt!) may want to look elsewhere.

The only other nit to pick is a short cord (nothing a good extension cord couldn't remedy).

It all comes down to needs and cost. If you need or really want more, well this isn't for you. If you're looking to walk before you run (so to speak), this is for you. The price is right, it's built to last, and if you outgrow it, you could recoup much of the cost.

I'll update the review as needed, but I'm very happy.
text_fidelity_b: Marcy Folding Motorized Treadmill/Electric Running Machine - Easy Assembly JX-650W
